footnote: AI illustrations, not real results. Real, consented study photos are required before any use.
image_prompt: Empty background scene only: a pure white seamless paper backdrop, soft daylight from the upper left, a faint grey contact-shadow area on the right. Square 1080x1080. Keep the right 45% of the frame as an empty space, evenly lit, for a pack photo placed later, and keep the left half as a calm empty area for copy. No product, no bottle, no packaging, no text, no letters, no logos, no people, no faces, no skin, no hands.
photography_needed: Real, consented, unretouched before/after photos from a documented study of this product (same person, light and framing), with the study's claim and duration on file.

verdict.detail: Change the flagged lines, or attach the substantiation a reviewer would need to accept them.

findings.message: The footnote says the visuals are AI illustrations standing in for results, so the ad shows skin outcomes nobody photographed, and a small-print disclaimer does not undo what the image shows (if the frames show clearer skin beside 'acne-prone', they also imply acne clearing, CLM-02). The rulebook rates CLM-15 as fix; my view is that this must not run until real evidence replaces the frames.
findings.fix: Replace the AI frames with real, consented, unretouched study photos carrying the study qualifier, or drop the result imagery and show the pack or texture instead; then rewrite or remove this footnote.

findings.span: Real, consented study photos are required before any use.
findings.message: This is an internal production instruction, not consumer copy, and it states outright that the creative is not cleared to run as built. Publishing it would print a team note on a paid ad and flag the visuals as placeholders.
findings.fix: Remove it from the creative, and resolve the imagery first (see the CLM-15 finding).
